title: A toy rewriter
prompt:
Write simplify(e). Simplify both children first, then apply these rules to the node, and keep re-applying them to the result until none fires. Integers are i32: fold with 32-bit wraparound.

  • Add(Const(a), Const(b)) becomes Const(a + b)
  • Mul(Const(a), Const(b)) becomes Const(a * b)
  • Add(Const(c), x) becomes Add(x, Const(c)) (x not a Const)
  • Mul(Const(c), x) becomes Mul(x, Const(c)) (x not a Const)
  • Add(x, Const(0)) becomes x
  • Mul(x, Const(1)) becomes x
  • Mul(x, Const(0)) becomes Const(0)
  • Add(Add(x, Const(a)), Const(b)) becomes Add(x, Const(a + b))
  • Mul(Mul(x, Const(a)), Const(b)) becomes Mul(x, Const(a * b))

Leave everything else alone. Add(Const(1), Add(Const(2), Var('y'))) becomes (y + 3), which takes three rules in a row. A match statement with class patterns, like case Add(Const(a), Const(b)):, reads almost exactly like this list.
hints: Write `rule(e)` that tries every rule once on a single node and returns the new node if one fired, or `None` if none did. Keep it separate from the walk over the tree.
Simplify both children first, rebuild the node, then call `rule` in a loop until it returns `None`. That's sources first plus a fixpoint.
Python ints never overflow, so fold with a wrap: `(x + 2**31) % 2**32 - 2**31`. Put the both-Const cases before the swap cases, so the swap only fires when the right side is not a Const.
explain: `rule` returns a rewrite or `None`, so the loop runs until no rule fires, and `simplify` runs it after simplifying the children: sources first, greedy, to a fixpoint. Folding wraps to 32 bits because Python ints would otherwise grow past i32. Because both-constant nodes fold before the swap rule is tried, moving a constant to the right can never ping-pong forever.
